chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Jo Jones as his idol, against Sonny Greer's flash
summary: Jo Jones became his idol; Sonny Greer was a flashy favourite, and Jo offered to send him to Omaha.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I'd see Duke's band, Sonny Greer, he was good with his -- all the chimes and things, but --
He was another one of my idols, a flashy player.
Yeah, Jo today says Sonny was wonderful, Jo always says --
Yeah, that's right. He gives Sonny a lot of credit.
Sure. He had his style, and that was it.
And the sock cymbal, he played with that sock cymbal. All I was doing then was (singing), just rhythm.
But he came up with all this flash, and I was just petrified. That was it. For me, that was it. Nobody else, Jo Jones. From then on, see?
: And, after all, he had a terrific influence on the whole scene.
So he said, 'I'm sending a band there to Omaha,' said, 'How would you like to go to Omaha? Have you ever been there?' I said, 'No, I've never been to Omaha.' So, he said, --
